svg.title: macOS · Project import · extracting · 760×680
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectImport.swift (ProjectImportSheet) over AppModel.archiveImport, presented from ContentView in App/LetsLapseApp.swift. The sheet a `.lapse` project archive puts up when it is opened from outside the app — a Finder double-click or "Open With", a drop on the Create screen, or the "Import a LetsLapse project…" row. Launch Services routes it here because App/Info.plist exports the type com.regularsteven.letslapse.project (extension `lapse`, conforms to public.data) and claims it with LSHandlerRank Owner + CFBundleTypeIconSystemGenerated, which is also what gives .lapse files their Finder icon. Presented from the ROOT, over any tab and over the blended-clip flow, because an import can start with no LetsLapse window in front of the human at all. Deliberately BLOCKING and not dismissable by clicking away (interactiveDismissDisabled): the extraction owns the disk for as long as it runs, and a shoot or a render started on top of it would fail for reasons neither could explain — Cancel (⎋) is always reachable, so it is never a trap. The bar is HAND-DRAWN, not ProgressView(value:): the system linear bar renders its fill in the control grey on macOS whatever the tint says. The denominator is the ARCHIVE'S OWN compressed size, hence "of about" — lzfse barely shrinks video and stills, and the true unpacked total is not known until the last entry lands; the tally itself counts payload bytes as each entry finishes (DirectoryArchive.extract's entry filter), so it never claims bytes that are not yet on disk. DESC-ONLY PHASES, not drawn here: (1) `.checking` — sizing the file and testing free space, indeterminate system linear bar in the accent, caption "Checking the file…"; (2) `.installing` — bar full, caption "Adding it to your library…", the moment the unpacked tree is renamed into ~/Library/Application Support/LetsLapse/Projects and library.json is rewritten. DRAWN AS VARIANTS: project-import.duplicate.svg (the archive is already in the library) and project-import.failed.svg. On success the sheet closes and the app lands on the imported project's DETAIL screen (requestedProjectDetailID), not in a blend flow: importing is "here is the thing", not "start editing it". Cancelling says nothing at all — the half-extracted tree is deleted and nothing joins the library. Verified 2026-08-13 by double-clicking a 2.37 GB archive from Finder on a cold launch; a real import of that size finishes in about two seconds on an M4 Max, so this sheet is frozen for screenshots with LL_IMPORT=checking|extracting|installing|duplicate|failed.
